text: {"question":"How do the generalized PAge parameterizations introduced in passage A compare with the CPL parametrization discussed in passage B regarding their effectiveness at reducing the Hubble tension when both cosmic microwave background and low‑redshift observations are included?","reference_answer":"The GPAge models, which extend the PAge framework to higher redshifts and improve low‑z accuracy, can significantly alleviate or even resolve the Hubble tension when CMB data are incorporated, and they are strongly preferred over ΛCDM. In contrast, the CPL parametrization, while showing a 3–4σ preference for an evolving dark‑energy equation of state in some DESI BAO analyses, only reduces the tension to about 2σ when combined with CMB data, and its early‑time modifications are not sufficient to fully resolve the discrepancy."}
